problems.title: Second largest

starter.python:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    # write your code here

main()

problems.statement:
Given n integers, print the second largest **distinct** value. If all values are equal (or n = 1), print -1.

Input
The first line has n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100000). The second line has n integers, each between -10^9 and 10^9.

Output
One integer.

solution.code:
import sys
d=sys.stdin.read().split();n=int(d[0]);a=set(map(int,d[1:1+n]))
s=sorted(a,reverse=True)
print(s[1] if len(s)>1 else -1)

problems.statement:
A string of brackets ( ) [ ] { } is balanced if every opening bracket is closed by the same kind in the right order. For each string print YES if it is balanced, otherwise NO.

Input
The first line has t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10). Each of the next t lines has one string of length 1 to 100000.

Output
t lines, YES or NO.

problems.title: Pairs with sum k

starter.python:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    a = list(map(int, data[2:2 + n]))
    # write your code here

main()

problems.statement:
Count the pairs of positions i < j with a[i] + a[j] = k.

Input
The first line has n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 200000, |k| ≤ 2·10^6). The second line has n integers, each between -10^6 and 10^6.

Output
The number of pairs (it can be larger than 2^31).

A solution that tries every pair is too slow for the largest tests.
